7.22.15.en: Let your soul love a wise servant [19], and do not deprive him of freedom [21].

7.22.16.en: A wise servant's enjoyment of freedom urges the children to care for learning and to behave wisely, as children of the Most High.

7.22.17.en: Ben Sira calls leaders and employers to recognize the value of the simple worker, the hired man, or the servant when he is faithful in his work, so that they may count him as their own self, and if he is a slave, that they set him free from bondage. For wisdom and prudence together with faithfulness in a person's life cannot be valued at any price.

7.22.18.en: The ancient systems gave the master freedom to do as he wished with the slave, and the slave had no right to defend himself. But the Law came requiring the master to restore the slave's freedom after six years of work and to treat him well (Ex 21:2; Lev 25:39; Deut 15:12-18).

7.22.19.en: Many slaves have gone ahead of their masters. The Apostle Paul appointed Onesimus, the slave who had stolen and run away from his master, as a bishop after he accepted the faith and lived in a spirit of godliness (see the Epistle to Philemon).

7.23.0.en: Have you cattle? Look to them, and if they are profitable to you, keep them [22].

7.23.1.en: The faithfulness of the wise man does not stop at the members of the family, or friends, or people in general, but extends to caring for the animals that he owns (Prov 27:23-27; Deut 25:4; Prov 12:10).

7.24.0.en: Have you children? Instruct them, make them obedient from their youth [23].

7.24.1.en: If the Lord calls us to care for animals, how much more must we care for our brothers among men. The Apostle Paul says: "Doth God take care for oxen? Or saith he it altogether for our sakes?" (1 Cor 9:9-10). The aim of discipline is that the children be marked by a spirit of obedience, so that they become like the Lord Christ when He was a boy, for He was obedient to St. Mary and Joseph the carpenter.

7.25.0.en: Have you daughters? Take care of their chastity, and do not show yourself too lenient toward them [24].

7.25.1.en: He who loves his daughter does not pamper her in a way that makes her lose concern and care for her chastity, but spares no effort that she may live pure until the day of her marriage. Some have been known for excessive pampering of their children, especially the wealthy, which spoils the happiness of the children themselves and deprives them of fulfilling their mission. Others have been marked by great harshness, especially where there are family problems. Therefore, firmness should be joined with tenderness, and with gentleness and tenderness firmness should be observed in moderation.

7.25.2.en: Some see that the care for daughters here is as for weak vessels, so that the parents do not put them to work that might rob them of their freshness and youth, which would affect them at their marriage. As for not being cheerful before them, perhaps what is meant is not to spoil their modesty by gatherings in which conversations take place that offend their modesty [20].

7.25.3.en: St. John Chrysostom warns the shepherds of the Church against pampering girls out of pity, lest the girls misunderstand the shepherds [21].

7.25.4.en: v Christ, the Educator of humanity, the divine Logos, calls us to spare no effort, with all strength and together with the gift of wisdom, to save our children by rebuke, discipline, calling them to account, warning them, and offering the remedy together with promises and gentleness toward them...

7.25.5.en: In short, God deals with us so that we ourselves may deal in this way with our children.

7.25.6.en: Have you children? Instruct them... Our children, whether male or female, you should love above everything else [22].

7.25.7.en: v In truth the Teacher of humanity, the divine Word, devotes Himself with all His power to save His little ones by every means through the plan of His wisdom: by warning, reproach, rebuke, correction, healing, promises, and giving benefits... In truth God deals with us as we deal with our children: we care for their bodies, and we do not show ourselves too lenient toward them. Yet we cherish a great love for our children, sons or daughters, more than love for anything else [23].

7.26.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria: Marry your daughter, and you will have done a great thing, but give her to a man of understanding [25].

7.27.0.en: Have you a wife after your heart? Do not divorce her, but do not trust yourself to a wife whom you hate [26].

7.27.1.en: He did not command the husband to love his wife, but indirectly made clear that his not loving her represents a danger to him. If the Law permitted divorce because of the hardness of their hearts, so that the husband would not act rashly toward his wife, here Ben Sira warns the husband against divorcing his wife out of his desire for a woman more beautiful than she. For the highest beauty is in wisdom, understanding, godliness, and good management. But if the husband feels that his wife is unfaithful, let him beware of her lest she deceive him and turn toward evil.

7.28.0.en: Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget your mother's pains in childbirth [27].

7.29.0.en: Remember that you were born of them; and what will you repay them for what they have done for you? [28]

7.29.1.en: There is no one who wishes for a person good, progress, and success more than they do. God granted the mother to labor with joy and delight for the sake of her children. God presents her love for her children as a likeness of His watchful care over us: "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee" (Isa 49:15).

7.30.s.en: 6. Uprightness of life and honoring the priests of the Lord

7.30.0.en: 31 Fear the Lord with all thy soul, and reverence his priests. 32 Love him that made thee with all thy strength, and forsake not his ministers. 33 Fear the Lord, and honour the priest. 34 And give him his portion, as it is commanded thee; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, 35 and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.

7.30.1.en: The discussion of man's relation to the priests of the Lord comes after the discussion of family life. This reveals the concept of the priesthood, whether in the mind of the priest or in the mind of the people.

7.30.2.en: One of the bishops of the Church of England asked me about the reason for the attachment of the youth in Egypt to the Church and the growing desire for consecration to the Lord, whether through the diaconate, the priesthood, or monasticism. My answer was: the first reason is our view of the priesthood. The believer looks upon the priest as a member with him in the same family, opening to him everything that touches his life as a son to his father. And the priest does not feel that he is an employee who demands an annual leave and is sent into retirement. For although it is the right of his family and his own right to spend a special period with the family, it is not as a personal right that he asks for it, but for the building up of himself and his family.

7.30.3.en: How my soul grieved when I called the pastor of the church in Los Angeles and said to him: "Reverend," and he answered me: I am now "Mr." because I have been retired!

7.30.4.en: The priest, even on his deathbed, intercedes for his people as his children, and even when he departs to Paradise he presents his children to the Lord that He may bless them and work in their lives. For this reason it is fitting for us to join what Sirach said, "uprightness of life and honoring the priests of the Lord," to the previous section concerning uprightness of family life.

7.30.5.en: Honoring the priest is realized in his imitation of the Lord Christ, "who washed the feet of His disciples," and in his sharing with his Church family, and indeed, if possible, in sharing the sufferings of every person. The greatness of the priest is not in an authority he demands, but in his attachment to the heavenly High Priest, who cares for the salvation of mankind and lifts them up to the heavenly mind.

7.30.6.en: Fear the Lord with all your soul, and honor His priests [29].

7.30.7.en: Ben Sira cared for the life of the Church, liturgical worship, and honoring the priests. He praised Aaron, the first high priest, as he praised the high priest of his own time, Simon son of Onias. The Lord did not will to give them a special portion in the Promised Land, but wished to distinguish them by being Himself their portion.

7.30.8.en: Ben Sira emphasized the obligation to give the priests their dues, because the spread of Hellenistic culture and the attraction of some to pagan philosophies had an effect on the priests' income, and some of them were compelled to work in farming.

7.30.9.en: Love Him who made you with all your strength, and do not forsake His ministers [30].

7.30.10.en: Fear the Lord and honor His priests, and give him his portion, as you have been commanded:

7.30.11.en: from the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things [31].

7.30.12.en: v He who honors the priest honors God also, and he who learns to despise the priest, in the course of time blasphemes God. He says: "Honor My priests" (see Sir 7:31). The Jews learned to despise God because they despised Moses and wanted to stone him. So he who moves with godliness toward the priest does this all the more toward God. And if the priest is wicked, God, when He sees you honoring him although he is not worthy of honor, rewards you for your honoring him [24].

7.31.s.en: 7. Divine love and our responsibility toward the forgotten

7.31.0.en: 36 And stretch thine hand unto the poor, that thy blessing may be perfected. 37 A gift hath grace in the sight of every man living; and for the dead detain it not. 38 Fail not to be with them that weep, and mourn with them that mourn. 39 Be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make thee to be beloved.

7.31.1.en: It is indeed good for a person to be generous with everyone, and to take part in burying the dead (Tob 1:17). Ben Sira also calls us to share the grief of the sorrowful and to visit the sick (Rom 12:15; Mt 25:39-40). Finally, a person's knowing that he is mortal keeps him humble (7:17; 28:6), along with offering due honor to one's neighbor.

7.31.2.en: Stretch out your hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected [32].

7.31.3.en: The Holy Bible cares for the forgotten groups who have no one to ask about them, and it requires kindness even toward the dead and the sick, so that the believer may bear witness to unbelievers that God is "the God of the forgotten, the suffering, the needy, and the oppressed." Let the believer's hand be stretched out in giving, and his heart in love toward unbelievers, as an ambassador of God, the Lover of mankind.

7.31.4.en: v [On the widow's mites and almsgiving]

7.31.5.en: Her love was greater than her offering, for love is better than whole burnt offerings... Therefore she overcame the rich with her offering. The priests of the people receive vows from those who offer abundantly, while the Lord of the priests sat down in a humility they did not perceive. The greedy chief priests care for sacrifices, but our Lord sought love within the soul... The Son of God rejoices in the one in whom there is love.

7.31.6.en: v The widow was able to know that the Most High has no need of an offering, but seeks a reason to enrich them.

7.31.7.en: She thought that if He had wished, He would have turned the dust into gold and the waters of the sea into coral, and she said to herself that He does not ask for gold out of need, but that people may share with Him by their offerings. For gold and silver are His, and as it is written, if the sacrifice is great and the love of the one who offers it is small, He rejects it. This woman alone knew how to discern and to offer with a pure heart a complete vow, with discernment... With pure love she knew how to offer! She offered her complete vow better than Jacob. For she did not set apart a tenth of her possessions, but this blessed woman loved the Lord more than herself!

7.31.8.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: Let her show the tenderness of giving in the presence of all the living; even to the dead let her not withhold kindness [33].

7.31.9.en: What does he mean by kindness to the dead? Caring for burying them with fitting honor, as Tobit used to do; caring for their families if they had debts; and giving alms to those to whom the dead man was kind.

7.31.10.en: Do not withdraw from those who weep, and grieve with the sorrowful [34].

7.31.11.en: The Apostle Paul says: "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep" (Rom 12:15). It may be easy for a person to grieve with the grieving and groan with his groaning, but it is hard for some to rejoice with the joy of their brother. This requires a lofty soul, so that he does not envy his brother for his success, but rejoices with him, counting every success of his brother as success for himself. The Apostle says: "And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular" (1 Cor 12:26-27).

7.31.12.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [Nothing establishes love so strongly as sharing in joy and sorrow. Because you are far from troubles, do not isolate yourself also from sharing with others. When your neighbor is in distress, count the distress as your own. Share his tears to support his contrite spirit, and share his joy so that the joy in him may become deep and rooted. Establish love, for by this you serve yourself more than you serve him. By your tears you become merciful, and by feelings of gladness you purify yourself of envy and gloom... If you cannot remove the evils from him, share with him by your tears, and you remove half of the evil; and if you cannot increase his good things, share his joy, and you add to him something great [25].]

7.31.13.en: Do not hesitate to visit the sick, for by such visits you will be beloved [35].

7.31.14.en: The Lord Christ counts the visiting of the sick as a visit to Himself, for He says: "I was... sick, and ye visited me" (Mt 25:36). As we desire the healing of the sick, it is fitting for us to desire for him also the fellowship of the eternal glories at the proper time.

7.32.0.en: 40 In all your works, remember your latter end; you shall never sin forever.

7.32.1.en: In all your affairs remember your latter end, and you will never sin [36].

7.32.2.en: The believer in all his works speaks of nothing, and nothing occupies his heart, so much as his entering into heaven. He becomes like Aaron the high priest, upon the skirts of whose robe round about golden bells were fastened. "And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and his sound shall be heard when he goeth in unto the holy place before the LORD" (Ex 28:35). So in every work he practices and in every matter he thinks about, what occupies him is his meeting with the Lord and his standing before the divine throne in the heavenly sanctuaries, where he enjoys the eternal glories and is in the company of the heavenly ones and in the fellowship of praise with them.

7.32.3.en: v Let him also have bells around the hem of his garment, for Holy Scripture says: when he enters the sanctuary he gives a sound and does not enter in silence (see Ex 28:35). These bells, which give a sound, were placed on the hem of the garment. Their purpose, as I believe, is that you must not be silent about the last things and the end of the world, but you must ring the bells continually and converse and speak according to what was said: "Remember your latter end, and you shall never sin" (Sir 7:36) [26].

7.32.4.en: Origen v says: "Remember your latter end, and you shall never sin" (Sir 7:36). For He who now forgives our sins will judge our sins on the day of judgment. He who died for us will appear again to judge all mankind [27].

7.32.5.en: St. John Chrysostom v [Speaking of Marcella]: "Remember your latter end, and you shall never sin" (7:36). This is like the precept of the sarcastic writer: "Live with death in your mind, and time flies"... She spent her days and always lived thinking that she would certainly die. Her very garments were as if reminding her of the tomb. And she offered herself a living sacrifice, reasonable, acceptable to God (Rom 12:1) [28].

7.32.6.en: St. Jerome v Question: How can we do everything for the glory of God?...

7.32.7.en: If we do everything according to God and His commandments, and do not seek the praise of men [29].

7.32.8.en: v "Arise, O Lord my God... in the commandment that You have commanded" (see Ps 7:8). This saying can also point to the mystery of the Resurrection, since the psalmist calls upon the Judge to arise to take vengeance on every sin and to fulfill the commandments that He had set for us... Do not take vengeance for me, but for Your commandment which You commanded, and they despised it" [30].

7.32.9.en: St. Basil the Great: Inspired by Sirach 7

7.33.s.en: Our heavenly Friend and brotherly love

7.33.0.en: v With the boldness of love Moses refused to move unless You, O Lord, went before the whole procession Yourself, for he said: "If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence" (Ex 33:15).

7.33.1.en: And behold, I call You, O my Savior, not only to accompany me, but to dwell within me.

7.33.2.en: Your presence, O my holy Friend, turns my depths into Your holy Kingdom.

7.33.3.en: It inflames my heart with longing for continual departure toward heaven with joy and exultation.

7.33.4.en: Your presence fills my depths with love for all my brothers, the sons of men.

7.33.5.en: By Your dwelling within me, I will not accept evil, and all iniquity departs from me.

7.33.6.en: The enemy of good cannot enter into my heart, my mind, and all my depths, and he will not dare to take hold of the steering wheel, for it is in Your hand!

7.33.7.en: v I will not desire a high position, nor temporal glory. And I will not boast of righteousness.

7.33.8.en: For everything that is holy is a gift from You, O righteous and holy One.

7.33.9.en: And if I fall into sin, You raise me up by Your fiery Spirit, and fortify my life so that I do not return to it.

7.33.10.en: My longsuffering heavenly Friend, I know Your forgiving mercies.

7.33.11.en: Behold, I ask for Your grace to fashion me, so that I may truly become a living icon of You!

7.33.12.en: v O You who accept gifts and offerings though You have no need of them. You call me: "My son, give me thine heart."

7.33.13.en: Receive my heart, and I will converse with You with an open heart. And let my prayer and all my worship ascend like the fragrant smell of incense, a place of Your delight and pleasure.

7.33.14.en: Let my prayer rise like a fire blazing with love.

7.33.15.en: And I will not cease giving, returning to You from what You have given me!

7.33.16.en: v Receive, O heavenly One, all my life and my movements, and allow me to walk in the steps of Your footprints.

7.33.17.en: In You I will not mock any person, whatever his weaknesses, for he may rise by Your grace, and I may fall through my foolishness!

7.33.18.en: I cherish Your friendship with me, O Truth, so that the devil, the father of liars, may have no authority over me!

7.33.19.en: v I will keep silence, especially in the presence of experienced elders.

7.33.20.en: Even in prayer, what concerns me is not much speaking and eloquence, but the language of the heart, unheard by men.

7.33.21.en: v I hope that I will not cease working even in my old age and sickness, for You do not take rest in the idle.

7.33.22.en: I will flee from the gatherings of sinners, where there is no place for You among them!

7.33.23.en: I will go about with You doing good, and I will gain friends for myself always!

7.33.24.en: v Enter, O heavenly Beloved, my house and dwell in the midst of the family.

7.33.25.en: My family is called by Your name, for I am Yours, my Beloved, and You are mine!

7.33.26.en: Be manifested in the life of the whole family, the old and the young.

7.33.27.en: Grant all love, wisdom, discernment, and prudence.

7.33.28.en: So that every member may desire to offer honor to the rest of the members!

7.33.29.en: v Grant me the spirit of simplicity, that I may see You in every priest and servant in Your Church!

7.33.30.en: v Let those whom You love be beloved to me.

7.33.31.en: I will care for the poor as Your little brother, and for the needy, the suffering, and the oppressed, for You declare that You are the God of the forgotten!

7.33.32.en: I will seek the lost and the outcast, that I may see You bring them back to Yourself and embrace them.

7.33.33.en: v Be with me until the last breath; prepare me before the agonies of death, and in the moments of death, and after death.

7.33.34.en: Open my insight, that I may see the heavenly sanctuaries awaiting my weakness and all my brothers!
